title: Orchid AI Ops - Launchpad Onboarding & Implementation Kickoff
next_steps: Redwood to share onboarding checklist + staging access guide by 2025-08-18
Customer to provide sample workload and token distribution CSV by 2025-08-20
Schedule first performance baseline run (SE + Marcus) for week of 2025-08-25
Security team follow-up: send SOC2 scope doc and KMS integration guide by 2025-08-19
action_items: Liam Chen - Create project in Console (staging org) and invite Orchid team - due 2025-08-18
Janelle Ortiz - Provide 2 representative prompts + expected QPS profile - due 2025-08-20
Priya Singh - Share list of compliance controls required (KMS, audit retention) - due 2025-08-19
Sofia Alvarez - Prepare quickstart runbook for prefix caching and batching - due 2025-08-22
meeting_header: Date: 2025-08-14 | Start: 16:00 PDT | Duration: 48 minutes | Recording: enabled
summary: Kickoff for Orchid AI Ops onboarding to Redwood. Covered scope of pilot (staging dedicated capacity), security requirements (KMS, audit logs, SSO), success criteria (latency SLAs and cost per 1k tokens), and operational handoffs. Agreed next steps for data/sample prompts, Console access, and an initial performance baseline run the week of 8/25.
topics: Private vs Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs
Security (KMS, audit logs, SSO/SAML, data residency)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Okay, great, good afternoon everyone, uh this is Maya from Redwood, thanks for joining. Well do intros quickly and then jump into the kickoff agenda.
[00:08] Janelle Ortiz: Hi, Janelle here — Head of MLOps at Orchid AI Ops. Thanks, Maya.
[00:12] Marcus Reed: Marcus, engineering manager, excited to get this rolling.
[00:15] Priya Singh: Priya, security lead. Ill be driving the compliance reqs.
[00:18] Lily (Guest): Ethan on the call as well.
[00:22] Maya Patel: Awesome. Quick note on structure: Liam will go through the onboarding checklist and Console invites, Sofia will cover the SE play for the perf baseline later. We want to clarify pilot scope and what success looks like.
[00:33] Liam Chen: (mm-hmm) Ill share screen for the checklist in a sec but high level — you asked for a staging Dedicated pool, isolated, with KMS for key management and audit logs retained for 90 days, is that right, Priya?
[00:45] Priya Singh: Yes, 90 days is our baseline, possibility to extend. Also SAML SSO is mandatory and we need user RBAC so devs only see token usage not KMS secrets.
[00:56] Maya Patel: Totally, Redwood supports SAML/SSO, RBAC roles, and RBAC can be scoped per project. The KMS integration we do via your cloud KMS or a customer managed HSM — theres a small config step in the Console.
[01:09] Priya Singh: When you say Console config, can the initial onboarding be done without exposing keys to Redwood operators? Thats a hard requirement.
[01:15] Sofia Alvarez: (joined) Sofia here—short answer: yes. We can set up the control plane so only the orchestration calls use wrapped keys; Redwood will not persist unencrypted key material. Theres a documented flow in the KMS guide. Ill send the exact diagram after the call.
[01:28] Janelle Ortiz: Cool, thanks. On the pilot: we want a week-long bench test with ~50 RPS sustained and spiky up to 120 RPS, mostly short prompts for routing decisions, and a few long-form summaries — how does Redwood recommend we size GPUs for that?
[01:44] Sofia Alvarez: For mixed short and long workloads we typically go with a multi-queue setup: smaller instances for low-latency short prompts and a few larger instances for large-context summarization. For Dedicated 4xA100 equiv is common for your QPS, but exact suggestion depends on token distribution — do you have a token histogram?
[01:58] Marcus Reed: Well pull the histogram, I have approximate numbers — median prompt 70 tokens, 95th percentile 1200 tokens for long summaries.
[02:07] Maya Patel: That helps. For cost predictability we can also pin a model variant with quantization profile; Redwood Optimize will suggest a config that trades 5-10% quality for 30-40% cost reduction in some cases. Is Orchid open to quantized variants during pilot?
[02:21] Janelle Ortiz: Possibly, but wed want to run A/B on quality. Were sensitive to hallucinations for the summary use-case.
[02:27] Sofia Alvarez: Absolutely — we can run canary rollouts with weighted traffic and circuit breakers, do quality checks. We also have eval hooks to run your prompt set and surface regressions.
[02:38] Ethan Wu: Quick sec — about caching, we have a lot of repeated prefixes; curious how prefix/KV caching works in practice.
[02:44] Sofia Alvarez: Good question. Redwood does automatic prefix caching at the request router; common prefixes are cached and served from GPU memory, reducing repeated compute. For your repeated routing signals itll cut cost and latency. Well include suggestions in the runbook.
[02:58] Marcus Reed: Sounds good. Timeline — wed like staging live within two weeks. Is that realistic?
[03:04] Liam Chen: Two weeks is tight but doable if we get the sample prompts, token distribution, SAML metadata, and a point-of-contact for net-new VPC connection. If Priya can share the SAML cert and Ethan can set up a staging VPC peering, we can target 2025-08-28 for a first smoke test.
[03:22] Priya Singh: I can get the SAML metadata by Tuesday. Concern: network egress rules — we need to ensure data never leaves our proximity. Can Redwood run in a private deployment in our VPC?
[03:31] Maya Patel: Yes, Redwood Private supports VPC-hosted control plane with no egress to shared infra. There are two paths: Private deployment (customer-managed control plane) or Dedicated with VPC peering + strict routing — Private on-prem gives the tightest controls. Which tier are you planning to evaluate for pilot?
[03:46] Janelle Ortiz: Wed like to try Dedicated isolated capacity first, with an eye toward Private if we move to production. Dedicated is faster to stand up.
[03:55] Maya Patel: Makes sense. Well document the pathway.
[03:58] (15:00) [Small side chat about calendar invites omitted]
[04:05] Liam Chen: Im going to list the immediate onboarding steps: 1) create staging org & invite users, 2) configure SAML SSO, 3) KMS setup, 4) network/VPC peering, 5) provide sample prompts + traffic profiles, 6) schedule SE baseline.
[04:20] Janelle Ortiz: That checklist covers it. Question about logs: how granular are audit logs? We need user-level action logs for compliance.
[04:28] Maya Patel: Audit logs include token use, API calls, config changes, and operator actions, all with user identity tied to SAML. Retention configurable; currently UI supports 90/180/365 days via add-on.
[04:39] Priya Singh: Ok good. Also encryption at rest for embeddings store — are embeddings stored encrypted separately?
[04:45] Sofia Alvarez: Yes, all persisted artifacts are encrypted and keys can be managed by your KMS. We support envelope encryption so Redwood doesnt have raw keys.
[04:53] Marcus Reed: For the SE baseline run — what metrics will you capture?
[04:57] Sofia Alvarez: Latency p50/p95/p99, throughput (RPS), GPU/offload utilization, token cost per 1k, and quality regressions vs your eval set. Well also capture KV cache hit rate.
[05:09] Ethan Wu: Do you have an API for streaming partial outputs? Our app relies on streaming for UX.
[05:13] Maya Patel: Yes, we support streaming responses, function/tool calling behavior and structured outputs. There are some considerations for batching and streaming interplay; Sofia will note best practices.
[05:24] Janelle Ortiz: Can Redwood integrate with our CI to automatically trigger regression evals on model rollouts?
[05:29] Sofia Alvarez: Yes, we have webhook hooks and an eval CLI that can be run in your CI to gate rollouts. You can set thresholds to automatically abort rollout if eval metrics degrade.
[05:38] Marcus Reed: Pricing question — what's the expected bill for the pilot? Ballpark is fine.
[05:42] Maya Patel: For a two-week staging pilot with Dedicated pool sized to your token profile, rough estimate is $6k-$12k for the pilot depending on GPU size and data egress. Well send a tailored estimate after we get the token histogram.
[05:56] Priya Singh: Well need a data processing addendum as well.
[05:59] Liam Chen: Noted, Legal will send DPA and DSA drafts; well include SOC2 attestation in the packet.
[06:06] (08:20) [brief network glitch, 5 seconds of audio drop]
[06:12] Maya Patel: Quick checkpoint — agreed items so far: staging org by 8/18, sample prompts by 8/20, baseline run week of 8/25. Any blockers?
[06:21] Priya Singh: The only potential blocker is internal approval for VPC peering in our security review, but were starting that now.
[06:27] Janelle Ortiz: Also request: can Redwood share a short runbook for troubleshooting timeouts and typical mitigation when KV cache misses spike?
[06:34] Sofia Alvarez: Yes, we have a KB article and a playbook — Ill attach that to the post-call notes.
[06:41] Marcus Reed: For monitoring — do we get Prometheus metrics or do we pull via Console API?
[06:46] Sofia Alvarez: Both. Console exposes metrics and traces; you can also hook into our metrics exporter for Prometheus ingestion.
[06:52] Ethan Wu: Great. On the topic of model versions — how are rollbacks handled if a rollout causes latency regressions?
[06:57] Maya Patel: Rollouts are incremental with automatic fallback. You can pin the previous model variant and the router will send traffic back. Rollbacks are immediate.
[07:05] (10:10) [short pause while notes updated]
[07:10] Janelle Ortiz: One more question about observability — can we get per-customer per-route cost breakdowns so our product team can map cost to features?
[07:17] Liam Chen: Yes, Console provides token-level billing breakdowns by route and model; well set up a cost dashboard for Orchid.
[07:24] Priya Singh: On identity mapping — we need to ensure service accounts are separated from human users with distinct RBAC.
[07:29] Maya Patel: Thats supported. We recommend service accounts with scoped tokens for CI and limited privileges.
[07:34] Marcus Reed: Okay looks like were aligned. Any other concerns on the security side?
[07:38] Priya Singh: Just to confirm: no plaintext data leaves our VPC unencrypted, and audit logs are write-once — thats required.
[07:45] Sofia Alvarez: We support encrypted in-transit and at-rest, and can enable append-only audit store for the pilot. Well document the exact retention and access controls.
[07:54] Janelle Ortiz: Thanks. Can we quickly walk the timeline and owners?
[07:58] Liam Chen: Sure — Ill read it: Liam to create staging org and invite users by 8/18; Janelle to send prompts and traffic by 8/20; Priya to send SAML metadata and compliance list by 8/19; Marcus + Sofia to run baseline week of 8/25. Redwood security to send SOC2 + KMS guide by 8/19.
[08:20] Maya Patel: Sounds good. Ill also add a short intro doc with the Console screenshots and how to accept invites.
[08:26] (12:00) [brief cross talk about internal calendars]
[08:32] Ethan Wu: One operational edge case — our load has short spikes (sub-100ms windows) which sometimes break autoscaling assumptions. How does Redwood handle burst capacity?
[08:41] Sofia Alvarez: Redwood Dedicated supports burst capacity and we can configure autoscaling policies with min warm nodes and preemptive spin-up to cover short spikes. For very short bursts we recommend keeping a small buffer of warm instances.
[08:55] Marcus Reed: Good. Any guidance for test harness? Well be running our own load generator.
[08:59] Sofia Alvarez: Well provide a suggested load script and token distribution file. Use the Console to run staged canaries and compare metrics.
[09:07] Janelle Ortiz: Ok lets finalize dates now: shall we tentatively set baseline run for Tuesday 2025-08-26 10am PT?
[09:13] Sofia Alvarez: Works for me. Marcus?
[09:16] Marcus Reed: Works.
[09:18] Priya Singh: Works if legal sign-off isnt blocking.
[09:21] Maya Patel: Well note it as tentative pending SAML and VPC.
[09:25] (15:00) [closing remarks]
[09:28] Maya Patel: Thanks, everyone — great kickoff. Ill follow up with the onboarding packet and links to the KBs. Any final questions?
[09:34] Janelle Ortiz: No, thats it for now. Looking forward to the run.
[09:37] Marcus Reed: Thanks all.
[09:38] Priya Singh: Thanks.
[09:40] Liam Chen: Bye all — talk soon.
[09:42] (End of recording)
